summary.text: Redox is a type of chemical reaction in which the oxidation states of the reactants change.
Oxidation is the loss of electrons and reduction is the gain of electrons, and the two cannot happen independently.
Redox chemistry drives rusting, combustion, cellular respiration, photosynthesis and batteries, and industry uses it to extract metals from their ores.

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: A blend of reduction and oxidation

facts.label: Reducing agent
facts.value: Loses electrons; also called an electron donor

facts.label: Oxidizing agent
facts.value: Gains electrons and is itself reduced

items.prompt: An iron nail rusts in moist air. Which statement about electrons is right?

options.label: Iron gains electrons and oxygen loses them
Iron and oxygen both lose electrons to the air
Iron loses electrons and oxygen absorbs them
No electrons move, since rusting is just drying out

items.explain: In rusting, the oxidation state of iron increases as it becomes an oxide, and oxygen is reduced as it absorbs the released electrons.

items.prompt: In a reaction, one substance donates electrons to another. What is it called, and what happens to it?

options.label: A reducing agent, and it is oxidized
A reducing agent, and it is reduced
An oxidizing agent, and it is oxidized
An oxidizing agent, and it is reduced

items.explain: The reducing agent loses electrons and is oxidized, while the oxidizing agent gains electrons and is reduced.

items.prompt: A chemist writes a reaction where one species is oxidized but nothing at all is reduced. What is wrong?

options.label: Oxidation needs oxygen, and none was written in
Oxidation and reduction occur together and cannot happen alone
Reduction must always happen one step before oxidation
Nothing is wrong, since each half-reaction can run alone

items.explain: Oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously and cannot occur independently. Two half-reactions always occur together to form a whole reaction.

items.prompt: A chemist adds hydrogen atoms across a C=C bond. In redox terms, what happened to the bond?

options.label: It was burned, because an oxide formed
It was left alone, since no oxygen was present
It was oxidized, because hydrogen was involved
It was reduced by taking on hydrogen atoms

items.explain: Oxidation is not only about oxygen. In hydrogenation, bonds such as C=C are reduced by the transfer of hydrogen atoms.

items.prompt: Originally, 'reduction' described heating a metal oxide ore to get the metal. What did the name refer to?

options.label: The ore losing weight as it became metal
The ore gaining weight as oxygen was added
The ore being cut into smaller pieces
The ore shrinking in volume as it cooled

items.explain: The word reduction first referred to the loss in weight when a metallic ore was heated, so ore was 'reduced' to metal.

items.prompt: A single electron moves from one species to another, and the process is described with redox couples and electrode potentials. Which class of redox reaction is this?

options.label: Atom transfer
Electron transfer
Hydrogenation only
Neither, since no oxidation states change

items.explain: Redox reactions fall into two classes. In electron transfer, a single electron usually flows from the species being oxidized to the one being reduced, often described with redox couples and electrode potentials.
